items.articleText: ABD borsasında roller değişti: Büyükler alıyor, küçükler satıyor - ABD borsalarında sert düşüşlerin ardından yatırımcıların stratejileri değişti. Bank of America verilerine göre, kurumsal yatırımcılar 6,1 milyar dolarlık alım yaparken bireysel yatırımcılar yaklaşık 2 milyar dolarlık satış gerçekleştirdi. ABD hisse senedi piyasalarında artan oynaklık, büyük yatırımcılarla bireysel yatırımcıların farklı yönlere hareket etmesine neden oldu. Bank of America'nın (BofA) yayımladığı verilere göre, son satış dalgasını fırsat olarak değerlendiren kurumsal yatırımcılar güçlü alımlara yönelirken bireysel yatırımcılar piyasadan çıkışlarını sürdürdü. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Bankanın verileri, kurumsal müşterilerin geçen hafta 6,1 milyar dolardan fazla hisse senedi satın aldığını ortaya koydu. Bu alımların yaklaşık 4 milyar dolarlık bölümünü hisse senedi borsa yatırım fonları (ETF) oluşturdu. Buna karşılık bireysel yatırımcılar üst üste dördüncü haftada da net satıcı konumunda kaldı. BofA'nın bireysel müşterileri aynı dönemde yaklaşık 2 milyar dolarlık hisse senedi sattı. Borsada alışılmış strateji tersine döndü Piyasalardaki bu ayrışma, son dönemde yatırımcı davranışlarında yaşanan değişime işaret ediyor. ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın 2 Nisan 2025'te açıkladığı ve "Kurtuluş Günü" olarak adlandırdığı tarife kararlarından bu yana bireysel yatırımcılar, piyasalardaki sert düşüşleri alım fırsatı olarak değerlendiriyordu. Ancak son satış dalgasında bu eğilim tersine döndü. Demokratların ABD ara seçimlerinde Kongre'nin her iki kanadında da kontrolü ele geçirmesiyle artan siyasi belirsizlik ve yapay zeka şirketlerinin büyüme beklentilerine ilişkin endişeler, piyasalardaki dalgalanmayı artırdı. Özellikle son yıllarda ABD borsalarındaki yükselişe öncülük eden teknoloji ve yapay zeka hisselerinde yaşanan satışlar, yatırımcıların risk iştahını olumsuz etkiledi. Bireysel yatırımcılar piyasaya destek vermeyi bıraktı RBC Capital Markets Türev Stratejisi Başkanı Amy Wu Silverman, CNBC'ye yaptığı değerlendirmede bireysel yatırımcıların geçmişte piyasa düşüşlerinde dengeleyici rol üstlendiğini ancak bu durumun değiştiğini söyledi. Silverman, bireysel yatırımcıların daha önce düşüşlerde alım yaparak geniş piyasa için destek oluşturduğunu, son dönemde ise bu desteğin ortadan kalkmasının ötesinde ters yönde bir hareket yaşandığını belirtti. Özellikle opsiyon piyasasında bireysel yatırımcıların artan tedirginliğinin fiyat hareketlerini hızlandırdığını ifade eden Silverman, bu davranışın piyasanın diğer bölümlerinde de zincirleme etki yarattığını kaydetti. Gözler kurumsal yatırımcıların hamlelerinde Yapay zeka bağlantılı hisselerdeki satışların etkisiyle S&P 500 endeksi geçen perşembe günü yüzde 4 gerilerken Nasdaq Bileşik Endeksi düzeltme bölgesine girdi. Endeksler daha sonra kayıplarının bir bölümünü telafi etse de piyasalardaki belirsizlik devam ediyor. Wall Street'in korku göstergesi olarak bilinen Cboe Volatilite Endeksi (VIX), çarşamba günü 18 seviyesi civarında işlem gördü. Önümüzdeki dönemde kurumsal yatırımcıların alımlarını sürdürüp sürdürmeyeceği ve bireysel yatırımcıların yeniden piyasaya dönüp dönmeyeceği yakından izlenecek. İki yatırımcı grubu arasındaki ayrışmanın kalıcı hale gelmesi, ABD borsalarındaki fiyat hareketlerinin yönü açısından belirleyici olabilir.

items.articleText: Borsada 5 şirketten peş peşe temettü açıklaması: Kararlar belli oldu Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 5 şirket, KAP üzerinden temettü kararlarını açıkladı. Şirketlerden biri kâr payı dağıtmama kararını kesinleştirirken, diğer 4 şirketin önerileri genel kurul onayına sunulacak. İşte o şirketler ve kararların gerekçeleri. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören şirketlerden temettü açıklamaları gelmeye devam ediyor. 11 Kasım Çarşamba günü Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan bildirimlerde Tuğçelik Alüminyum, Cosmos Yatırım Holding, Zedur Enerji, Albayrak Hazır Beton ve Casa Emtia'nın 2025 yılına ilişkin kâr dağıtım kararları ve önerileri duyuruldu. Beş şirketin de nakit veya bedelsiz pay şeklinde kâr payı dağıtımı öngörmediği açıklanırken, Cosmos Yatırım Holding'in kararı genel kurulda kabul edildi. Diğer dört şirketin temettü dağıtmama önerileri ise genel kurul onayına sunulacak. Tuğçelik Alüminyum ve Metal Mamülleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş., 2025 yılına ilişkin kâr payı dağıtımı yapılmaması yönündeki yönetim kurulu teklifini KAP'a bildirdi. Şirketin Türkiye Finansal RaporTuğçelik Alüminyum (TUCLK)lama Standartları'na (TFRS) göre hazırlanan finansal tablolarında 127 milyon TL net dönem zararı oluşurken, yasal kayıtlarda 22,8 milyon TL net dönem kârı hesaplandı. Yönetim kurulu, yasal yedekler ayrıldıktan sonra kalan tutarın geçmiş yıllar kâr ve zararları hesabına aktarılmasını ve temettü dağıtılmamasını önerdi. Karar, 2 Aralık 2026 tarihinde gerçekleştirilecek genel kurulun onayına sunulacak. Cosmos Yatırım Holding (COSMO) Cosmos Yatırım Holding, 2025 yılı kârının geçmiş yıllar zararları hesabına aktarılması yönündeki yönetim kurulu önerisinin 11 Kasım'da yapılan genel kurulda kabul edildiğini duyurdu. Şirketin SPK düzenlemelerine göre hazırlanan finansal tablolarında 7,29 milyon TL net dönem kârı bulunmasına rağmen, geçmiş yıllar zararları nedeniyle net dağıtılabilir dönem zararı 127,97 milyon TL olarak hesaplandı. Alınan karar doğrultusunda pay sahiplerine nakit veya bedelsiz temettü ödemesi yapılmayacak. Zedur Enerji (ZEDUR) Zedur Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş., 2025 yılı hesap dönemine ilişkin kâr payı dağıtılmaması yönünde yönetim kurulu kararı aldığını açıkladı. Şirketin bağımsız denetimden geçmiş finansal tablolarında 20,73 milyon TL net dağıtılabilir dönem kârı hesaplanırken, Vergi Usul Kanunu kapsamında tutulan yasal kayıtlarda 70,22 milyon TL zarar oluştu. Yasal kayıtlarda dağıtılabilir kâr bulunmaması nedeniyle temettü ödenmemesi yönündeki teklif, 15 Aralık 2026 tarihinde yapılacak olağan genel kurulda pay sahiplerinin onayına sunulacak. Albayrak Hazır Beton (ALBTN) Albayrak Hazır Beton Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş., 2025 yılına ilişkin kâr payı dağıtmama önerisini KAP'a bildirdi. Şirketin TFRS'ye göre hazırlanan finansal tablolarında 14,99 milyon TL, yasal kayıtlarında ise 38,11 milyon TL net dönem kârı oluştu. Yönetim kurulu, işletme sermayesi ihtiyaçları, yatırım ve finansman gereksinimleri ile mali yapının güçlendirilmesi hedeflerini dikkate alarak kârın dağıtılmamasını önerdi. Bu kapsamda, yasal yedekler ayrıldıktan sonra TFRS'ye göre 13,09 milyon TL, yasal kayıtlara göre ise 36,21 milyon TL tutarındaki kârın şirket bünyesinde tutulması planlanıyor. Temettü dağıtılmaması yönündeki teklif, 4 Aralık 2026 tarihinde yapılacak genel kurulda görüşülecek. Casa Emtia (CASA) Casa Emtia Petrol Kimyevi ve Türevleri Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş., 2025 yılı finansal sonuçlarında zarar oluşması nedeniyle kâr payı dağıtılmaması yönünde karar aldığını duyurdu. Şirketin SPK düzenlemelerine göre hazırlanan finansal tablolarında 131,19 milyon TL, yasal kayıtlarında ise 97,02 milyon TL net dönem zararı oluştu. Yönetim kurulu, 2025 yılına ilişkin nakit veya bedelsiz temettü dağıtılmaması önerisinin olağan genel kurulda pay sahiplerinin onayına sunulacağını açıkladı. Temettü kararlarında genel kurul süreci 11 Kasım'da açıklama yapan beş şirketin tamamı 2025 yılına ilişkin kâr payı dağıtmamayı öngörüyor. Ancak şirketlerin gerekçeleri farklılık gösteriyor. Tuğçelik Alüminyum, Zedur Enerji ve Casa Emtia'nın açıklamalarında finansal tablolardaki zararlar veya yasal kayıtlarda dağıtılabilir kâr bulunmaması öne çıkarken, Albayrak Hazır Beton kârını yatırım ve finansman ihtiyaçları için şirket bünyesinde tutmayı planlıyor. Cosmos Yatırım Holding'de temettü dağıtılmaması kararı genel kurulda kesinleşirken, diğer şirketlerde nihai karar genel kurul toplantılarında verilecek.

items.titleTr: Missing 11-month-old baby found buried alive in a crate in South Carolina
items.summaryTr: Officials say the child was found close to his father's home on Tuesday, a day after he was taken, and is being cared for in hospital.
items.articleText: Missing 11-month-old baby found buried alive in a crate in South Carolina - Published An 11-month-old baby has been rescued in South Carolina after officials say he was buried alive in a crate by his father. Koah Sharpe had been missing since Monday when he was taken by his father, Michael Comer, 25, according to the Lexington County Sheriff's Department. Comer was arrested on a burglary charge on Monday evening but his son was not with him. The baby was found on Tuesday "buried alive" and "clinging to life" not far from his father's house, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours. The child is now in hospital receiving care, Koon said, adding he was hopeful he would make a full recovery. Police are still deciding what further charges to bring against the father. The search for baby Koah began on Monday after his father took him from his mother's house. Comer's mother was watching the child and had left her son alone with him briefly, Koon said, when he left abruptly with Koah. Comer was seen travelling to multiple locations without the baby and was later arrested in Lexington County without Koah. A search party of 100 police and fire department officials were then sent to search for the child, the sheriff said. He added that when they asked Comer where his son was, he "did not have much to say" about his whereabouts. Koon said that rescuers searched the woods near Comer's father's house and saw some "freshly disturbed dirt". As they began to dig, they heard a baby crying - something the sheriff described as "the most joyful sound you ever heard". "The race was on. Everybody was getting down there trying to get him out," Koon added. He said the crate was wrapped in a towel that probably provided enough air for Koah to survive for as long as he did, while the cold weather kept him from getting too hot. "The crate was, probably, I'm guessing about a two-foot [61cm] by two-foot dog crate. So, I think, once that crate hit the ground, he was probably up at least a foot from the top of that crate to the top of the ground," Koon explained. Of the parents relationship, the sheriff said there were "obviously some issues". Comer had previously pleaded guilty to domestic violence charges, court records show. Comer's mother, Patricia Comer, told NBC News that Koah's mother had full custody of him but allowed her to supervise while her son watched him. She said her son had watched the baby before unsupervised without any problems. "Honestly, I'm his mother, and I never expected this from him," Patricia Comer said.

The baby was found on Tuesday "buried alive" and "clinging to life" not far from his father's house, Lexington County Sheriff Jay Koon said at a news conference. It is thought he had been there for 24 hours. The child is now in hospital receiving care, Koon said, adding he was hopeful he would make a full recovery. Police are still deciding what further charges to bring against the father. The search for baby Koah began on Monday after his father took him from his mother's house. Comer's mother was watching the child and had left her son alone with him briefly, Koon said, when he left abruptly with Koah. Comer was seen travelling to multiple locations without the baby and was later arrested in Lexington County without Koah. A search party of 100 police and fire department officials were then sent to search for the child, the sheriff said. He added that when they asked Comer where his son was, he "did not have much to say" about his whereabouts. Koon said that rescuers searched the woods near Comer's father's house and saw some "freshly disturbed dirt". As they began to dig, they heard a baby crying - something the sheriff described as "the most joyful sound you ever heard". "The race was on. Everybody was getting down there trying to get him out," Koon added. He said the crate was wrapped in a towel that probably provided enough air for Koah to survive for as long as he did, while the cold weather kept him from getting too hot. "The crate was, probably, I'm guessing about a two-foot [61cm] by two-foot dog crate. So, I think, once that crate hit the ground, he was probably up at least a foot from the top of that crate to the top of the ground," Koon explained. Of the parents relationship, the sheriff said there were "obviously some issues". Comer had previously pleaded guilty to domestic violence charges, court records show. Comer's mother, Patricia Comer, told NBC News that Koah's mother had full custody of him but allowed her to supervise while her son watched him. She said her son had watched the baby before unsupervised without any problems. "Honestly, I'm his mother, and I never expected this from him," Patricia Comer said.

items.summary: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.

items.titleTr: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
items.summaryTr: Talks in Abu Dhabi centred around Europe's security framework, with US envoys due to meet Putin and Zelensky on Thursday.
items.articleText: Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough - Published Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day. Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion. However, both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon. Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest." "I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible. Comments by Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky were less conciliatory. "Right now... a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the US, and on whether Europe comes to its senses," he said. After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky. The meetings in Abu Dhabi had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe. For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member. For Moscow, a reworked "security framework" is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion. Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while the Kremlin's Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system. That framework would serve as "a new Yalta and Potsdam", Medinsky said, referring to the 1940s summits in which the victorious Allied powers carved up post-war Europe into spheres of influence. Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin. Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them. Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent. Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday. Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin. There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted. Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added. Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are essential to its security. Moscow, meanwhile, has never backed down from its demand that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds. "Every inch" of land would be "returned to Russia one way or another", Medinsky said. Kushner acknowledged that the territorial question remained the hardest, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region. Later, Budanov admitted the talks had been "tough" and that Ukraine's priority was to ensure Russia could not attack it again. "These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this." Related topics - Published1 day ago - Published22 hours ago

items.title: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years
items.summary: Protests are also expected in the biggest cities less than three weeks before Spaniards vote in parliamentary elections.

items.titleTr: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years
items.summaryTr: Protests are also expected in the biggest cities less than three weeks before Spaniards vote in parliamentary elections.
items.articleText: Spain sees widespread disruption in first general strike for 14 years - Published Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption in the first general strike for 14 years called by the main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Demonstrations have taken place across the country, including in Madrid and Barcelona, where tens of thousands marched in the evening. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." However, the Spanish Confederation of Business Organisations said participation was "low and uneven", depending on the areas and sectors involved. Some of the biggest disruption on Wednesday was seen in the main industrial hubs of Madrid and the north-eastern region of Catalonia where traffic was halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have soared in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50m sq apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460 (£2,056). That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. "Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. Read more - Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage - Published23 September - Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests - Published5 October The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike." Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. "It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas." He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible." With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible". However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. "This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%.

items.articleText: Satın alma onaylandı: Dev havayolu şirketi resmen satılıyor! Artık borsada olmayacaklar - EasyJet hissedarları, ABD'li Apollo'nun 5,7 milyar sterlinlik satın alma teklifini onayladı. AB incelemesinin ardından işlemin 2027'nin ilk çeyreği bitmeden tamamlanması hedefleniyor. Satış gerçekleşirse easyJet Londra Borsası'ndan ayrılacak. ABD merkezli özel sermaye şirketi Apollo'nun, İngiliz düşük maliyetli hava yolu easyJet'i 5,7 milyar sterlin karşılığında satın alma teklifi hissedarlar tarafından onaylandı. İşlemin gelecek yılın ilk çeyreği sona ermeden tamamlanması hedefleniyor. Hissedarların yüzde 97'sinden fazlası destekledi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle EasyJet'in açıklamasına göre, oylamada temsil edilen hisselerin yüzde 97,07'si satın alma anlaşması lehine oy kullandı. Oy hakkına sahip hissedarların yüzde 83,29'u da teklifi destekledi. Böylece şirketin özel mülkiyete geçerek borsadan ayrılması için gereken hissedar onayı eşiği aşılmış oldu. AB incelemesi bekleniyor Hissedar onayının ardından satın alma işlemi, Avrupa Birliği'nin düzenleyici kuralları kapsamında incelemeye alınacak. EasyJet, işlemin gelecek yılın ilk çeyreği sona ermeden tamamlanmasını hedefliyor. Satışın tamamlanması halinde easyJet, 25 yılı aşkın süredir işlem gördüğü Londra Borsası'ndan ayrılacak. İşlem, Avrupa'da bir hava yolu şirketine yönelik en büyük özel sermaye satın almalarından biri olmaya hazırlanıyor.

items.summaryTr: Borsa İstanbul'da 6 şirket yeni iş ve yatırım gelişmelerini duyurdu. Hareket Proje'nin 4,5 milyon dolarlık anlaşmaları, Orge Enerji'nin 276 milyon TL'lik sözleşmesi ve Türkiye Kalkınma Bankası'nın 250 milyon euroluk kredisi öne çıktı.
items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul’da 6 şirketten KAP açıklaması: Milyarlık anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar Borsa İstanbul'da 6 şirket yeni iş ve yatırım gelişmelerini duyurdu. Hareket Proje'nin 4,5 milyon dolarlık anlaşmaları, Orge Enerji'nin 276 milyon TL'lik sözleşmesi ve Türkiye Kalkınma Bankası'nın 250 milyon euroluk kredisi öne çıktı. Borsa İstanbul'da işlem gören 6 şirket, 11 Kasım Çarşamba günü yeni sözleşme, iş ilişkisi, yatırım ve finansman gelişmelerini Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. Açıklamalarda milyonlarca dolarlık anlaşmalar, jeotermal enerji yatırımı ve 250 milyon avroluk kredi öne çıktı. Hareket Proje (HRKET): 4,5 milyon dolarlık iki ayrı anlaşma Hareket Proje Taşımacılığı ve Yük Mühendisliği, Kazakistan ve Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri'ndeki projeler kapsamında ağır nakliye ve vinç kiralama hizmetleri için 2,5 milyon dolarlık anlaşma imzaladı. Şirket ayrıca vagon taşımacılığı ve proje kargo taşımacılığı hizmetleri için iki ayrı sözleşme yaptı. Üç ay sürmesi planlanan bu projelerin toplam bedeli 2 milyon dolar olarak açıklandı. DCT Trading (DCTTR): 34,8 milyon TL'lik pamuk alım anlaşması DCT Trading, 2026-2027 sezonu yurt içi pamuk alımları kapsamında 34 milyon 775 bin TL tutarında anlaşma imzaladı. Emlak Konut GYO (EKGYO): 315 bağımsız bölüm için ruhsat alındı Emlak Konut GYO'nun İstanbul Esenler Oruçreis 2. Etap projesinde, Güzelbahçe Defne Evleri kapsamında 295 konut ve 20 ticari üniteden oluşan toplam 315 bağımsız bölüm için yapı ruhsatları alındı. Orge Enerji (ORGE): 276 milyon TL'lik veri merkezi sözleşmesi imzalandı Orge Enerji, Ankara'da inşası devam eden Veri Merkezi Projesi'nin ilk etap elektrik işlerine ilişkin sözleşme sürecini tamamladı. Şirketin 4 milyon 950 bin euro + KDV tutarındaki teklifi için işverenle sözleşme imzalandı. 23 Eylül 2026 tarihli TCMB kuru üzerinden yaklaşık 275 milyon 974 bin TL + KDV değerindeki işin 10 ayda tamamlanması planlanıyor. Kocaer Çelik (KCAER): İtalya merkezli şirketle jeotermal santral anlaşması Kocaer Çelik'in yüzde 99 iştiraki Kocaer Enerji, İtalya merkezli Exergy International ve Türkiye iştiraki Exergy Turkey ile santral tedarik sözleşmesi imzaladı. Sözleşme, Aydın'ın Buharkent ve Kuyucak ilçelerinde geliştirilen Kocaer-1 Jeotermal Enerji Santrali'nin ilk fazını kapsıyor. 12,34 MWe brüt kurulu güce sahip santral için ORC teknolojisine dayalı ekipmanların tasarımı, mühendisliği, imalatı ve tedariki gerçekleştirilecek. Türkiye Kalkınma ve Yatırım Bankası (KLNMA): KfW ile 250 milyon euroluk kredi Türkiye Kalkınma ve Yatırım Bankası, Alman Kalkınma Bankası KfW ile 250 milyon euro tutarında kredi anlaşması imzaladı.

items.title: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.summary: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.

items.titleTr: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
items.summaryTr: The US Department of Justice says the men were involved in a string of plots, including a major incident near the UK airbase that is used by US armed forces.
items.articleText: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says - Published The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives that it alleges were involved in a string of plots in the US and Europe. The DOJ said Iranian agents most recently "orchestrated a terrorist plot at an air force base in the United Kingdom", saying they were involved in the major incident in September near RAF Fairford in the UK, where US armed forces were stationed. The three men have been accused by the DOJ of being involved in 18 attacks and attempted attacks, including in London, Amsterdam and Paris. Some of the incidents were said to be directed by the men over FaceTime. The DOJ said they acted in the name of the group Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI). Iranian Mohsen Mohajeri, Iraqi national Mohammad Ali al-Hassani and dual Iranian-Iraqi citizen Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi were charged in an indictment unsealed on Tuesday, the DOJ said. The DOJ said that most recently, al-Hassani "orchestrated a terrorist plot" at RAF Fairford - where on 27 September a major incident was declared after suspicious vans were reported near the base. Seven men have been arrested in the UK over the incident at RAF Fairford. Iran has strongly denied any involvement. Al-Hassani and Mohajeri were allegedly both in Iran at the time of the incident, the indictment claims. Meanwhile, al-Saadi was coordinating with the pair through third parties from a prison in New York, where he is awaiting trial on previous charges after being arrested in August, it adds. US court records show that al-Saadi is due in court on 19 November, though it is not clear whether this status conference - which is usually a routine scheduled appearance - relates to the new charges or the previous ones. The BBC has asked the Southern District of New York for comment. Mohajeri and al-Hassani are not in custody, two sources told the BBC's US partner CBS News. The BBC has asked the DOJ for comment on the suspected whereabouts of the two men not in US custody. In the DOJ's statement detailing the indictments, it said: "Of the 18 terrorist attacks in the spring of 2026 for which HAYI claimed responsibility in Europe, seven took place in the UK." It added that the attacks involved "arsons, explosives, and in one instance, a near-fatal stabbing in London of two Jewish men, including a dual US-British citizen". Two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, in April. A suspect is due to stand trial next year. The indictment also details an arson attack on a Jewish charity in London on 17 April, which allegedly saw al-Hassani "directing" an individual over FaceTime. On 17 April , a building previously used by Jewish Futures, an educational charity, was set alight in Hendon, north-west London. The following day, the DOJ said al-Hassani participated in another video call with an individual carrying out an attack on a synagogue in London. On 18 April, Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow was targeted in an arson attack. A 17-year-old boy pleaded guilty to the incident earlier this year. The indictment also claims the three were involved in attacks on the Bank of New York Mellon building in Amsterdam on 15 March and on the Bank of America building in Paris on 28 March. It added that the trio tried to carry out attacks on "Jewish institutions in the US", including attempting to target a synagogue in Manhattan, New York in March or April. "This eight-count indictment shows the determination of Iran to commit terrorist attacks in Europe and the US," FBI Director Kash Patel said. He added that one of the three "allegedly sent coded messages to assist in future acts of violence" from detention. Patel said the accused were involved in nearly 20 attempted attacks in support of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah. RAF Fairford A major incident was declared on 27 September near the UK's RAF Fairford base, in the Cotswolds in Gloucestershire, after three suspicious vans were seen near the airbase. No explosive materials were found in the vans, but a quantity of petrol was seized. The DOJ said that in August, al-Hassani "allegedly directed and paid associates" in the UK to "conduct preparatory steps and arrange logistics for the RAF Fairford terrorist plot". On 22 August, al-Hassani paid one individual to "perform pre-operational surveillance of RAF Fairford's perimeter", the department said. In September, al-Hassani paid several people to help him prepare for the plot, the DOJ also alleged. According to its statement, this included "procuring vans and barrels of fuel, researching the purchase of chemical accelerants, including large quantities of potassium chloride, and purchasing metallic objects that could be used as explosive shrapnel". The suspects then gave the vans an appearance of being used by a fuel delivery business and a swimming pool supply business, the DOJ stated. "On 26 September, al-Hassani allegedly tasked individuals to drive three vans, some of which were later determined to contain barrels of fuel, to the RAF Fairford base." The DOJ also said al-Hassani was "in frequent communication" with the van drivers and helped to direct them where to drive. "At least two of the three vans, while en route to the perimeter of RAF Fairford, encountered a security roadblock and were not allowed to proceed on their intended route," it added. It was in the very early hours of 27 September, that the vans were spotted by a local farmer who was heading home from a party, and called the police. The Iranian embassy in London has said it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident. Two British nationals appeared in court last month in connection with the alleged Iran-linked plot. The US withdrew all its bombers from RAF Fairford after the incident, with President Donald Trump citing "some threats" to the base as the reason. RAF Fairford has been used by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades. In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from there to the Middle East for "defensive" strikes on Iran. In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces". items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul'da bir şirket TERA Fondaki hisselerini TMSF’den aldı - Blume Metal, tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 lot kendi hissesini TMSF'den pay başına 29,40 TL'ye satın aldı. İşlem sonrası şirketin elindeki payların sermayeye oranı yüzde 1,73'e yükseldi. Blume Metal Kimya A.Ş. (BLUME), Tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 adet kendi payını Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu'ndan (TMSF) satın aldı. İşlem, pay başına 29,40 TL kapanış fiyatı üzerinden gerçekleştirildi. 497 bin 693 lotluk hisse alımı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yapılan açıklamaya göre TMSF, tasfiye sürecindeki Tera Fon'da bulunan 497 bin 693 lot BLUME payının öncelikle şirket tarafından satın alınmasını teklif etti. Blume Metal, yatırımcıları korumak ve ileriye dönük yatırım amacıyla söz konusu payları 11 Kasım 2026 tarihinde, 29,40 TL kapanış fiyatı üzerinden satın aldı. Şirketin elindeki payların oranı yüzde 1,73'e çıktı Açıklamada, işlemin pay geri alımı için ayrılan tutar dışındaki kaynaklardan karşılandığı belirtildi. Satın alma işleminin ardından Blume Metal'in sahip olduğu kendi paylarının nominal tutarı 3 milyon 33 bin 847 adede ulaştı. Bu payların şirket sermayesine oranı ise yüzde 1,73 olarak açıklandı.

items.articleText: Huang skandalı Nvidia'yı sarstı! Hisseler çakılmıştı, Morgan Stanley desteğini çekti - Nvidia hisseleri, Jensen Huang hakkındaki iddiaların ardından yaşanan iki günlük düşüşü çarşamba günü yüzde 3,95'lik yükselişle telafi etmeye çalıştı. Yatırımcılar, soruşturmanın şirketin faaliyetlerine ve 17 Kasım'daki bilançosuna etkisini izliyor. Nvidia hisseleri, CEO Jensen Huang hakkındaki iddiaların şirketin faaliyetlerine olası etkileri tartışılırken iki günlük düşüşün ardından çarşamba günü yükseldi. Yatırımcılar, skandalın şirketin işlerine ve yapay zekâ yatırımlarına yansıyıp yansımayacağını değerlendiriyor. İki günlük düşüşün ardından yüzde 3,95 yükseldi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Nvidia hisseleri çarşamba günü yüzde 3 civarında yükselerek önceki iki işlem günündeki kayıpların ardından toparlandı. Hisse senedi pazartesi günü yüzde 4,3, salı günü ise yüzde 5,47 değer kaybetmişti. Düşüşte, Nvidia Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Jensen Huang'ın Çin istihbaratıyla bağlantılı olduğu öne sürülen bir kişiyle ilişkisine dair iddiaların şirkete olası etkileri belirleyici oldu. Nvidia, salı günü şirket sırlarının veya ulusal güvenliğin tehlikeye girip girmediğini araştırmak üzere Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz hukuk bürosuyla anlaştığını duyurdu. Yatırımcılar üç olası senaryoyu değerlendiriyor Bank of America, salı günü yayımladığı değerlendirmede gelişmelerin Nvidia üzerindeki etkisine ilişkin üç senaryoya dikkat çekti. İlk senaryoda krizin sınırlı kalması ve şirket yönetiminde devamlılığın korunması öngörülüyor. İkinci senaryoda ise belirsizliğin uzaması ve bilanço öncesinde şirketin değerlemesi üzerinde baskı oluşturması ihtimali bulunuyor. Üçüncü senaryoda soruşturmanın olumsuz sonuçlanması, yönetimde değişiklik yaşanması veya daha sıkı kısıtlamaların gündeme gelmesi halinde şirketin finansal görünümünün yeniden değerlendirilmesi gerekebileceği belirtiliyor. Zacks Baş Stratejisti John Blank ise satışların arkasında iki temel endişe bulunduğunu söyledi: ABD'nin gelişmelerin ardından yeni kısıtlamalar getirmesi ve iddialar hakkında yeni sorunların ortaya çıkması. Blank, CNBC'ye yaptığı değerlendirmede gelişmelerin Nvidia, Jensen Huang ve genel olarak yapay zekâ yatırımları açısından olumsuz olduğunu ifade etti. Morgan Stanley, Nvidia'yı en beğendiği hisseler listesinden çıkardı Morgan Stanley, çarşamba günü Nvidia'yı en beğendiği hisseler listesinden çıkardı. Bankanın bu kararı, Nvidia hisselerinin 2 Ekim'de listeye alınmasından bu yana yüzde 25'ten fazla değer kaybetmesinin ardından geldi. Analistler, Huang'ın liderliğinin Nvidia'nın stratejik yönü açısından kritik önem taşıdığını vurguladı. Şirketin üçüncü çeyrek finansal sonuçlarını 17 Kasım'da açıklaması bekleniyor. Huang'ın soruşturma sürerken ofise dönerek olağan iş akışını sürdürmeye çalıştığı, salı günü de toplantılarına devam ettiği bildirildi.

items.title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats
items.summary: Bessent is now one of several Trump administration officials to live on military bases due to safety concerns.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats
items.summaryTr: Bessent is now one of several Trump administration officials to live on military bases due to safety concerns.
items.articleText: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats - Published US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports. CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal. Bessent has been at the forefront of efforts to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a wider economic blockade. While the exact nature of the threats against Bessent remain unclear, US intelligence has warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans, including US officials. "After the Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase," a source told CBS. Georgetown is an affluent part of Washington that is home to a number of government officials and prominent residents. Those security concerns, the source added, prompted authorities to move Bessent to a military base in the area. In a statement, a Treasury Department spokesperson said only that Bessent "will not be deterred" by threats and "remains committed" to the US effort to pressure Iran's economy. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment. In September, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans. The New York Times has reported that the Iranian effort includes the targeting of current and former US officials. One source told the newspaper this has "reached a more advanced stage". Other US officials reportedly on Iran's list of potential targets include former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former National Security Advisor John Bolton and Mark Milley, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Milley and Bolton's security teams were taken away by the Trump administration shortly after he returned to office last year. Bessent is one of a number of administration officials that live on military bases. The White House's new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, was moved to a base in late 2025 - before the conflict with Iran began. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both live on military bases, as did former Attorney General Pam Bondi and former intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard. The US and Israel launched an air campaign against Iran in February, killing its leader and prompting the regime in Tehran to retaliate with strikes on US allies across the region and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and gas usually travels. In June, the US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a blockade targeting Iranian ports. Related topics - Published1 day ago

items.title: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
items.summary: The news comes at a turbulent time for Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
items.summaryTr: The news comes at a turbulent time for Prabowo, who faces a growing rift with his predecessor Joko Widodo.
items.articleText: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying - Published Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power. It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid. The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran. The aide, Budi Arie, said Gibran's resignation letter was submitted directly to Prabowo on Wednesday. It remains unclear if it has been accepted. Gibran has long faced controversy over whether his high school qualifications met legal requirements to run for office. Having studied in Singapore and Australia, he had used an Indonesian equivalence certificate to demonstrate his educational credentials. Indonesian law requires vice-presidents to have completed senior secondary school or its equivalent, but the Supreme Court found no evidence to prove Gibran had graduated. "No evidence was found to show Gibran had a foreign diploma or certificate that could serve as the basis for equivalency with a senior high school or equivalent qualification," it said. It also considered a Constitutional Court ruling from earlier in October which came to the same conclusion. Gibran previously argued that undertaking university education was sufficient proof that he had completed senior high school. On Tuesday, he asked for the chance to challenge the ruling and be given the opportunity to prove the legitimacy of his education credentials, State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said. Gibran's ascension to Prabowo's ticket in the 2024 election was part of an alliance formed between his father, outgoing president Joko Widodo - known as Jokowi - and Prabowo, his erstwhile bitter rival. Gibran was 36 at the time, and only became eligible for candidacy after a controversial ruling by the Constitutional Court, which exempted him from the minimum age requirement of 40. His resignation comes as tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo appear to have flared. Since taking the presidency, Prabowo has shown little interest in pushing ahead with Jokowi's legacy project: the construction of Nusantara, a new capital. Instead, he has focused much of the state's resources on his own flagship programme to provide free school meals across the country. In a series of personnel reshuffles over the past year, Prabowo has also shifted many Jokowi loyalists into new roles, including long-serving finance minister Sri Mulyani Indrawati. Last week, authorities arrested presidential chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo - no relation - on suspicions of wiretapping the president. Prabowo sacked Listyo a day later, in what many pointed to as a sign of a crumbling alliance: Listyo, who formerly served as the national police chief, is widely considered a long-time ally of Jokowi. Within the government, allegiances seem to be shifting. On Monday, three members of Prabowo's cabinet collectively resigned from the party led by Kaesang Pangarep, Jokowi's youngest son, citing their desire to focus on their duties in Prabowo's administration. All this is unfolding at a particularly turbulent period in Prabowo's presidency. The free school meals programme is struggling for funding, parts of Indonesia have recently battled the country's worst wildfires in a decade, and the national stock market faces crisis amid allegations of widespread market manipulation. On Tuesday, students across the country staged demonstrations to protest against the government's handling of a range of issues, including the environmental crisis and corruption.

items.summaryTr: Sarar Şirketler Grubu, hakkında çıkan iflas iddialarını yalanladı. Şirket, gündeme gelen hukuki uyuşmazlığın aile bireyleri arasında yaşandığını, grup şirketlerinin mali durumuyla ilgisi bulunmadığını ve faaliyetlerin kesintisiz sürdüğünü açıkladı.
items.articleText: Türkiye’nin 82 yıllık giyim markası iflas mı etti? Şirketten iddialara yanıt geldi - Sarar Şirketler Grubu, hakkında çıkan iflas iddialarını yalanladı. Şirket, gündeme gelen hukuki uyuşmazlığın aile bireyleri arasında yaşandığını, grup şirketlerinin mali durumuyla ilgisi bulunmadığını ve faaliyetlerin kesintisiz sürdüğünü açıkladı. Türkiye'nin 82 yıllık giyim markası Sarar, hakkında çıkan iflas iddialarına ilişkin açıklama yaptı. Sarar Şirketler Grubu, gündeme gelen hukuki sürecin aile bireyleri arasındaki şahsi uyuşmazlıklardan kaynaklandığını belirterek şirketlerin herhangi bir iflas sürecinin içinde olmadığını bildirdi. İflas iddialarının ardından şirketten açıklama CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Sarar ailesinin üyeleri arasında şirket gelirlerinin paylaşımından kaynaklanan anlaşmazlık nedeniyle iflas yoluyla takip başlatıldığı yönündeki haberlerin ardından şirketten açıklama geldi. Sarar Şirketler Grubu, söz konusu sürecin grup şirketleriyle bağlantılı olmadığını vurgulayarak, haberlerde yer alan iddiaların aile bireyleri arasındaki şahsi nitelikteki uyuşmazlıklardan ibaret olduğunu belirtti. "Mali açıdan güçlü ve istikrarlı yapımızı koruyoruz" Şirket açıklamasında, aile bireyleri arasındaki hukuki anlaşmazlıkların Sarar Grup şirketlerinin mali durumuyla ilişkilendirilmemesi gerektiği ifade edildi. Açıklamada, "Sarar Grup şirketleri bahsi geçen sürecin bir parçası değildir. Haberlere konu edilen hususlar, şirketlerimizin mali durumu ile ilgisi bulunmayan, aile bireyleri arasındaki şahsi nitelikteki iddia ve uyuşmazlıklardan ibarettir" denildi. Şirketlerin mali açıdan güçlü ve istikrarlı yapısını koruduğu belirtilen açıklamada, ticari, operasyonel ve kurumsal faaliyetlerin olağan şekilde ve kesintisiz devam ettiği kaydedildi. "İflas algısı oluşturulması gerçeği yansıtmıyor" Sarar, aile içindeki hukuki uyuşmazlıkların marka ve şirketlerin mali durumuyla ilişkilendirilmesine de tepki gösterdi. Açıklamada, şirketler hakkında bir iflas süreci bulunduğu yönünde gerçeğe aykırı algı oluşturulmamasının önem taşıdığı vurgulandı.

Açıklamada, "Sarar Grup şirketleri bahsi geçen sürecin bir parçası değildir. Haberlere konu edilen hususlar, şirketlerimizin mali durumu ile ilgisi bulunmayan, aile bireyleri arasındaki şahsi nitelikteki iddia ve uyuşmazlıklardan ibarettir" denildi. Şirketlerin mali açıdan güçlü ve istikrarlı yapısını koruduğu belirtilen açıklamada, ticari, operasyonel ve kurumsal faaliyetlerin olağan şekilde ve kesintisiz devam ettiği kaydedildi. "İflas algısı oluşturulması gerçeği yansıtmıyor" Sarar, aile içindeki hukuki uyuşmazlıkların marka ve şirketlerin mali durumuyla ilişkilendirilmesine de tepki gösterdi. items.articleText: Bitcoin hovers near $74K as stocks rise despite US bond yield rebound Bitcoin traded in a narrow range as investors bought the dip in tech stocks and US bond yields climbed on high CPI inflation data. Bitcoin (BTC) circled $74,000 at Wednesday’s Wall Street open as stock markets rallied and US bond yields surged. Key points: - Bitcoin failed to follow US stocks higher as CoreWeave gained up to 21% after beating Q3 revenue estimates. - The US 10-year bond yield hit a high of 5.02% on the back of higher-than-expected US CPI inflation. - BTC traded in a narrow range between its 21-week and 50-week trend lines at $73,078 and $75,492, respectively. Tech stocks rise while 10-year yield returns to 5% Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD diverging from US equities as investors resumed buying the dip in tech stocks. BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The AI sector led the day’s early gains, with cloud-computing company CoreWeave jumping over 20% after reporting better-than-expected Q3 revenue and lifting its 2026 guidance. CoreWeave stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Nvidia, which suffered on Monday and Tuesday amid ongoing controversy over CEO Jensen Huang, opened around 2.5% higher. Nvidia stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Oil prices, meanwhile, gained on the day amid fading optimism over a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war. As attacks on ships traversing the Strait of Hormuz continued, analysis pointed to several practical hurdles to restoring pre-conflict traffic levels, even if a deal is reached. “Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to take the risk,” LSEG Oil Research wrote in a note on Tuesday, according to Reuters. US WTI crude oil was up 1.4% on the day at $87.70 per barrel after dropping to $84 on Tuesday, its lowest since late August. Brent crude gained 1.5% to $93.40. CFDs on WTI crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Stocks rose even after Tuesday’s higher-than-expected Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation data pushed US bond yields sharply higher. The 10-year yield returned to 5% on Wednesday for the first time since Oct. 29, while the 30-year yield reached as high as 5.378%, a level last seen on Oct. 22. US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, said that bonds were pricing in a more hawkish approach to interest rates by the US Federal Reserve. Markets have priced in a 0.25% rate hike in December, with the odds of a 0.5% move now increasing. “Inflation breakevens today are focused on the drop in oil prices while regular Treasuries today are reacting to a Fed that is definitely going to hike next month, as of now, with one another in January,” Boockvar told CNBC. Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today BTC price stays between two key trend lines Bitcoin continued to trade in a narrow range between its 21-week and 50-week simple moving average at $73,078 and $75,492, respectively. Volatility cooled as traders awaited a new catalyst after the CPI report. BTC/USD one-day chart with 21-week and 50-week SMAs. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Investor profitability suffered as Bitcoin lost support around $75,700, the aggregate cost basis of the short-term holder (STH) cohort - entities holding a given amount of BTC without selling for up to 155 days. On Tuesday, STH wallets sent over 47,000 BTC to exchanges at an unrealized loss, potentially signaling an increase in panic selling if those coins were sold.

items.titleTr: Protesters gather in Spain for first general strike in 14 years
items.summaryTr: Thousands are protesting across Spain over housing and the high cost of living.
items.articleText: Protesters gather in Spain for first general strike in 14 years Transport and other public services across Spain have faced serious disruption on Wednesday in the nation's first general strike in 14 years. The main unions called the strike over housing and the high cost of living, with demonstrations planned across the country. It comes nearly two weeks before Spain's parliamentary elections, which will be held on 29 November. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. The BBC's Nick Beake reports from the protest in Madrid.

items.titleTr: Enflasyonu doları uçurdu! Dört haftanın zirvesi görüldü: Piyasanın gözü cuma gününde
items.summaryTr: ABD'de beklentileri aşan enflasyon verisi doları dört haftanın zirvesine taşıdı. Fed'in aralık ayında faiz artırması beklenirken, cuma günü açıklanacak ÜFE verisi doların yeni yönünü belirleyebilir.
items.articleText: Enflasyonu doları uçurdu! Dört haftanın zirvesi görüldü: Piyasanın gözü cuma gününde - ABD'de beklentileri aşan enflasyon verisi doları dört haftanın zirvesine taşıdı. Fed'in aralık ayında faiz artırması beklenirken, cuma günü açıklanacak ÜFE verisi doların yeni yönünü belirleyebilir. ABD'de beklentilerin üzerinde gelen enflasyon verisi doların küresel piyasalarda son dört haftanın en yüksek seviyesine çıkmasını sağladı. Fed'in aralık ayında faiz artıracağı beklentisi güçlenirken, cuma günü açıklanacak Üretici Fiyat Endeksi (ÜFE) verisi doların yönü açısından kritik önem taşıyor. Fed'in faiz artırımı beklentisi doları destekledi CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle ABD'de salı günü açıklanan tüketici enflasyonu verilerinin beklentileri aşması, doların diğer önemli para birimleri karşısında değer kazanmasına yol açtı. Verilerin ardından Fed'in aralık ayındaki toplantısında 25 baz puanlık faiz artırımına gideceği beklentisi güçlendi. Piyasalarda daha yüksek oranlı bir faiz artışı ihtimali de yakından izleniyor. Dolarda yeni yükseliş için 50 baz puanlık artış beklentisi DHF Capital S.A. analisti Bas Kooijman, doların yükselişini sürdürebilmesi için Fed'in 50 baz puanlık faiz artırımı yapacağına yönelik beklentilerin güçlenmesi gerekebileceğini belirtti. Kooijman, aralık ayında 25 baz puanlık artışın zaten temel senaryo olduğunu, doların daha fazla değer kazanması için yarım puanlık faiz artışı ihtimalinin daha güçlü fiyatlanması gerektiğini ifade etti. Gözler cuma günü açıklanacak ÜFE verisinde Kooijman'a göre cuma günü açıklanacak ABD Üretici Fiyat Endeksi (ÜFE) verisi, doların seyrinde belirleyici olabilir. ÜFE'nin beklentilerin üzerinde gelmesi veya Fed yetkililerinden sıkı para politikasını destekleyen açıklamaların gelmesi doların yeni kazançlar elde etmesini sağlayabilir. Buna karşılık verilerin zayıf kalması durumunda doların son dönemdeki yükselişinin bir bölümünü geri vermesi beklenebilir.

items.summary: Clients can store and transfer Bitcoin, Ether and select stablecoins through the bank, which manages their wallets and private keys.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Deutsche Bank launches crypto custody for companies and institutions
items.summaryTr: Clients can store and transfer Bitcoin, Ether and select stablecoins through the bank, which manages their wallets and private keys.
items.articleText: Deutsche Bank launches crypto custody for companies and institutions Clients can store and transfer Bitcoin, Ether and select stablecoins through the bank, which manages their wallets and private keys. Germany’s largest lender, Deutsche Bank, launched its crypto custody service for institutional and corporate clients on Wednesday, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph. The bank also signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, its majority-owned asset manager, to explore collaboration on tokenized money market funds, crypto asset exchange-traded commodities and stablecoins. Deutsche Bank announced plans to offer the service to institutional and corporate clients in Europe on Sept. 16, pending regulatory clearance. Deutsche Bank’s listing for crypto custody and transfer services in the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register is dated Oct. 12 and names Germany’s BaFin as its regulator. The service initially supports Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and select stablecoins, including Circle’s USDC (USDC) and EURC (EURC), as well as AllUnity EURAU. Gerald Podobnik, co-head of Deutsche Bank’s corporate bank, told Reuters in October that the bank planned to launch in Germany before expanding to Asian financial centers in 2027. Deutsche Bank partnered with crypto infrastructure provider Taurus in 2023 to develop custody services after applying for a digital asset custody license in Germany. Related: Deutsche Bank-backed AllUnity launches Swiss franc stablecoin CHFAU

items.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Barclays’ BlackRock Bitcoin ETF holdings rose 48% in the third quarter, pro-crypto lawmaker Tom Emmer was elected House Republican minority whip as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress and hotter-than-expected US inflation raised concerns about a potential half-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December. Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). Its reported IBIT holdings also rose 50% to about 521,000 shares, from 347,000 at the end of June. The filings offer an early indication of changing institutional Bitcoin ETF ownership, with more major banks and hedge funds yet to disclose their third-quarter positions. Institutional investment managers have until Monday to file their third-quarter holdings reports. Crypto ally Tom Emmer elected House GOP minority whip Pro-crypto US Representative Tom Emmer has been elected House Republican minority whip, securing the party’s second-highest leadership position as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January. Emmer beat Texas Representative August Pfluger in a 103-76 secret ballot vote, according to Politico. He previously served as House Republican majority whip and will remain the party’s No. 2 leader, this time under incoming Minority Leader Jim Jordan. As minority whip, Emmer will be responsible for rallying Republican votes, coordinating the party’s legislative strategy and helping maintain unity on key bills. “Tom has been one of the strongest advocates for digital assets in Congress, and he has led the fight against a government-controlled CBDC and stood up for American innovators,” GOP Senator Cynthia Lummis said on X. Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.”

items.articleText: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline. The collapse of Paraguay’s digital lender Ueno Bank last week left nearly three million customers — roughly 60% of Paraguay’s adults — unable to access their accounts. Paraguay’s Central Bank placed Ueno into resolution on Nov. 3 after its solvency ratio fell below half the legally required minimum. An investigation uncovered questionable lending practices and deficiencies in credit documentation and accounting. The collapse also triggered a political crisis, with thousands taking to the streets to protest and President Santiago Peña attempting to resign before being impeached and arrested on charges of breach of trust and using his office for personal gain. Paraguay’s peer-to-peer crypto market immediately reflected the turmoil, with some sellers asking for a USDt premium of up to 13%. “USDt is a lifeline for hundreds millions of people in the world,” Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said. For many, the incident sparked uncertainty over savings, wages and the money needed to cover everyday expenses. With the local guaraní (PYG) currency falling 12.3% in a week, some turned to stablecoins to maintain the value of their funds, or just to keep payments moving along. David Eisenmann, founder and chief executive of Paraguayan crypto exchange X4T, tells Magazine the timing made the liquidity need even more pronounced. “The intervention came in the first days of the month,” he says, “exactly when salaries, rent and supplier invoices are due,” adding that many business owners “couldn’t make payroll.” For some, USDt was “suddenly the most liquid money” they had: “This week they learned that having an account isn’t the same as having access to your money.” But beyond another TradFi masterclass in the virtues of self-custody, Ueno’s collapse highlights the growing role of dollar-pegged stablecoins providing an alternative source of liquidity when traditional banks fail. Crypto as a source of liquidity Eisenmann says X4T processed more than $10 million in local on-ramp volume over the 30 days to early November, but some of that activity predated Ueno’s collapse. “The dollar began recovering against the guaraní in October,” he says, “and the Ueno news sped up a move that was already underway.” Related: Stablecoins can drain from banks and nations at lightning speed He says the activity “runs in both directions,” with some customers selling crypto for guaraníes or dollars to cover payments they could no longer make through Ueno, while “demand for USDt and USDC as a dollar store of value has risen sharply.” Paraguay’s Central Bank placed Ueno into resolution on Nov. 3. Source: Central Bank of Paraguay As of Nov. 9 the Central Bank said 93.1% of customers with Ueno deposits had been repaid. Despite this confidence has been shaken and X4T continued to see higher online inquiries for dollar-denominated stablecoins. In fact, Eisenmann says the level “has not changed significantly” from the week of the collapse. Rhys Hicks, associate analyst at data and analytics company GlobalData, says the digital bank’s failure has shown “how much can go wrong when governance does not keep pace with growth.” That said, he’s not seeing evidence of a mass migration from Paraguayan banks into stablecoins, since other banks “picked up the slack,” and people “seem to have been angrier” with the government than with the banks. “Some consumers will look for different ways to keep their money safe, but I do not see an overwhelming shift to stablecoins yet,” he says. An old impulse, with new rails Seeking dollars when confidence in domestic banks falters is hardly new. In Argentina’s 2001 financial crisis, the government imposed the “corralito,” restricting cash withdrawals from bank accounts, following a run on deposits. Related: Peter Thiel backs crypto-friendly Silicon Valley Bank rival — Report Amid a deepening crisis over the country’s currency peg and sovereign debt, the government later converted dollar-denominated deposits into pesos, reducing people’s savings by about 30% overnight and further damaging confidence in the country’s fraying banking system. Tether CEO calls USDt a lifeline. Source: Paolo Ardoino But stablecoins aren’t decentralized and they are not insulated from the banking system either. During the March 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, stablecoin issuer Circle disclosed that $3.3 billion of USDC reserves, around 8% of the total, were held at the lender. USDC briefly depegged and fell to 86 cents on secondary markets after Circle said it could not withdraw the funds. A BIS paper on stablecoins and the international monetary system warns that widespread use of dollar-backed tokens could create challenges for monetary sovereignty in emerging markets. Hicks says stablecoins can provide an alternative during periods of political instability and “low trust in the local system” because they are pegged to a more stable currency, like the US dollar. But regulators need to address “transparency” and “consumer protection,” he says, because stablecoin holders don’t benefit from the same deposit guarantees as bank customers, and there is no central bank to step in and make them whole. Eisenmann says he expects the incident to spark more “diversification,” with people “spreading their money across banks, cash and digital assets” instead of relying on a single institution. “How quickly trust in the banks returns will depend on how quickly and transparently the authorities handle the resolution,” he says. items.titleTr: Bitcoin Covenants Part 5: MATT and OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY — How Bitcoin could carry state across transactions
items.summaryTr: OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs.
items.articleText: Bitcoin Covenants Part 5: MATT and OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY — How Bitcoin could carry state across transactions OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs. This is Part 5 in the technical article series about Bitcoin covenants by Cointelegraph Research. To read the previous article click here. MATT (Merkleize All The Things) is a smart contract framework for Bitcoin that enables stateful contracts and scalable fraud proofs. A stateful contract carries information forward across multiple transactions and can update this information as the contract evolves. Standard Bitcoin scripts do not provide this capability, because each transaction is evaluated independently with no memory of previous executions. Every covenant proposal allows state-carrying UTXOs to an extent, as illustrated by scripting languages such as Sapio, which builds on OP_CTV. This works by using addresses to represent a finite state automaton, where transactions function as the state transitions. However, there is no way to elegantly implement numerical logic in this paradigm, a gap filled by MATT, and in particular its proposed implementation through OP_CCV. Because MATT allows committed data to be computed at spend time and re-embedded into the next output, each spend can derive a new state dynamically, instead of choosing from a predetermined set of states. How OP_CCV commits state into a Taproot key To understand the MATT proposal, it is useful to first review how Taproot commits data through public keys. Every Taproot output contains a base public key, called the internal key, which can be cryptographically modified or “tweaked” to commit to extra information. Formally, the tweaked public key is Q = P + t·G, where P is the internal key, G is the generator of the secp256k1 elliptic curve, and t is a tagged hash of P and the committed data. In a regular Taproot output, this commitment typically encodes the Merkle root of a taptree, which contains hidden spending paths. MATT builds on this mechanism to also embed contract state into the key. Instead of embedding complex logic directly in Bitcoin’s scripting language, MATT encodes computation as a sequence of state commitments, and the chain verifies only that each state transition is valid. MATT can be realized through different opcode combinations. The most direct and well-specified implementation relies on OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY (OP_CCV). OP_CCV provides the primitive that makes state-carrying UTXOs feasible within Taproot. OP_CCV allows a script to verify that a Taproot input or output key has been tweaked to commit to a specific piece of state data. The internal key is first tweaked with a hash of the contract’s current state, and then Taproot’s standard taptree tweak is applied on top. The resulting output key therefore commits to both the tapscript (the set of spending conditions) and the current state of the contract. OP_CCV can then enforce what state is carried forward into the next output. It allows the script to inspect the state data provided on the witness stack, perform computations on it, and require that the resulting updated state is correctly re-committed in a specified output. This is how state transitions are enforced on-chain. The stack format is: OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY The opcode supports three modes for checking an output as well as a separate input mode. In default mode, the entire BTC value of the input UTXO is allocated to the specified output; in deduct mode, only a portion equal to the output’s amount is assigned, leaving the remainder available for further outputs; and in ignore mode, the script and data commitment are verified without constraining the amount. Because default and deduct modes are designed to preserve value across checked outputs, transaction fees must be paid through separate fee-paying inputs. A dedicated fee input and change output can be added to the transaction without conflicting with the covenant’s constraints. This prevents the accidental burning of funds that can occur in more primitive covenant implementations, such as OP_CTV or SIGHASH_ANYPREVOUT. It also addresses a major limitation of presigned-transaction-style covenants, which typically define amounts upfront and therefore cannot accommodate dynamic fee adjustments or partial unvaults. OP_CCV + OP_CAT: Merkle Proofs and Fraud Proofs When OP_CCV is combined with OP_CAT, the full MATT framework becomes even more expressive. OP_CAT enables byte concatenation in Script, which makes it possible to construct and verify Merkle proofs directly on-chain. Two distinct Merkle trees are associated with a Taproot output in such an arrangement. The first is the familiar Taproot script tree (the taptree), whose leaves are the contract’s spending scripts. The second is a separate state tree, whose leaves are the contract’s data, such as the intermediate steps of a computation. The OP_CCV + OP_CAT script can verify a Merkle proof against the current state tree root, compute the updated root after a transition, and use OP_CCV to force the next output to commit to it. This construction enables fraud-proof systems with a slashing condition in which a long computation is committed off-chain, and only the specific disputed step (with its path in the binary tree) needs to be revealed and verified on-chain. Similar systems exist as optimistic rollups on other blockchain systems: the full computation runs off-chain, and the on-chain contract only intervenes when someone raises a challenge. Fraud proofs require that the computation be compiled down to a binary circuit or equivalent step-by-step representation that can be committed to in a Merkle tree. OP_CCV + OP_CAT would avoid the need for the Lamport one-time signatures and pre-signed transaction graphs that BitVM relies on to enforce state consistency. Beyond fraud proofs, the OP_CCV and OP_CAT combination also has implications for vaults. OP_CCV alone can implement vaults, but when combined with OP_CAT, it allows fully featured vaults that are essentially equivalent to the functionality proposed by OP_VAULT. As James O’Beirne, the author of OP_VAULT, has noted, OP_CCV represents a more general and robust design that effectively supersedes his earlier proposal. In the next article in this series, we will move on from general covenant proposals to review application-specific opcodes such as OP_VAULT, OP_UNVAULT, and OP_EVICT. Each of the opcodes are designed to solve a specific problem rather than provide broad programmability. Magazine: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?

items.titleTr: CoreWeave stock jumps 15% premarket after Q3 revenue beats estimates
items.summaryTr: CoreWeave’s third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion, beating analyst estimates by 3.4%. Its revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion.
items.articleText: CoreWeave stock jumps 15% premarket after Q3 revenue beats estimates CoreWeave’s third-quarter revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion, beating analyst estimates by 3.4%. Its revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion. CoreWeave shares jumped 15.27% in premarket trading Wednesday after the AI cloud provider reported third-quarter revenue that beat analyst estimates. The shares traded at $56.12 as of 12:50 pm UTC, trimming the stock’s year-to-date decline to 32%, according to Yahoo Finance. CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in third-quarter revenue after the market closed on Tuesday, up 168% from $1.36 billion a year earlier. Revenue came in about 3.4% above the $3.54 billion consensus estimate compiled by Google Finance. The company also reported a revenue backlog of about $132.5 billion as of Sept. 30. The figure includes revenue CoreWeave expects to recognize under existing customer contracts, subject to delivery and service availability. In April, CoreWeave announced a multiyear agreement with AI developer Anthropic to provide computing capacity for its Claude models. Days later, CoreWeave signed a $6 billion deal with quantitative trading company Jane Street to supply cloud infrastructure for trading and research. CoreWeave started as a crypto miner and began shifting to AI infrastructure in 2019. Related: CoreWeave shows how crypto-era infrastructure quietly became AI’s backbone

items.summary: The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators.

items.titleTr: FSB urgest Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules
items.summaryTr: The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators.
items.articleText: FSB urgest Turkey to tighten crypto oversight, set stablecoin rules The Financial Stability Board cited progress on crypto licensing and urged stronger enforcement and cooperation with foreign regulators. The Financial Stability Board (FSB) urged Turkey to tighten its oversight of crypto markets and adopt dedicated rules for stablecoins. In a peer review published on Wednesday, the global financial watchdog said Turkish authorities had made progress by introducing registration and licensing requirements for crypto service providers. The report was part of the FSB’s regular program of country reviews and assessed Turkey’s progress in implementing the board’s 2023 global recommendations on crypto and stablecoins. It followed a broader 2025 review that found gaps in how jurisdictions had implemented those recommendations. The FSB recommended that Turkey begin monitoring crypto-related risks to financial stability under a formal framework, strengthen supervision and enforcement, and improve cooperation and information sharing with foreign regulators. Turkey’s Capital Markets Board introduced licensing and operational requirements for crypto exchanges and custodians in March 2025, including minimum capital thresholds. The FSB said Turkey had introduced safeguards including requirements to segregate assets held in custody and a ban on domestic crypto payments. The safeguards help limit the spread of crypto-related risks to banks and payment systems. Authorities also launched a centralized platform to monitor crypto activities. The FSB’s 2025 review found that Turkey had finalized rules for crypto assets but lacked a dedicated stablecoin framework. In June 2025, Turkey’s Finance Ministry outlined plans to introduce additional transaction checks and limits on stablecoin transfers to combat money laundering. Related: Turkey tightens crypto rules with source, purpose checks on transfers
